body.statement:
In the binary-response specialization of Lee and Gu (2026), double
triangularity under their standing BLCM conditions makes both triangular-view
conditional tables and their observable two-view probability matrix have rank
\(2^K\), and it identifies \(K\) against alternative BLCMs with fewer than
\(K\) binary latent coordinates.

source.locator: Theorem 1, Lemma 1, and displayed equation (3) in Section 3.1 of arXiv version 2
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1 (Identifying K). For each j, let Xj be a nondegenerate separable metric space. Suppose that the true Γ-matrix is double triangular. Then, the number of latent variables K is identifiable. Lemma 1. Consider a BLCM with binary responses. Suppose that the Γ-matrix corresponding to X1,…,XK is lower-triangular. Then, the 2^K × 2^K conditional probability table P(X1:K | H) has full column-rank. Lemma 1 implies that P(XS1 | H), P(XS2 | H) have full column rank of 2^K. Additionally, the diagonal matrix diag(π) also has full rank 2^K. Thus, P(XS1,XS2) has rank 2^K.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the authors arXiv v2 HTML, Theorem 1, Lemma 1, and equation (3) discussion, lines 240–257, accessed 2026-09-12.
